key_insight: Trustworthy protein–ligand binding predictions require trustworthy evaluation. These guidelines emphasize transparent data, code and experimental procedures, with safeguards against data leakage and bias.
problem_solved: Data leakage, biased benchmarks and opaque evaluation procedures can inflate reported performance and undermine fair comparisons between structure-based scoring methods.
method: Make evaluation data, code and experimental procedures transparent to support reproducibility.
Apply safeguards against data leakage and bias when designing benchmarks and evaluations.
Use fair, consistent evaluation practices to compare protein–ligand scoring methods meaningfully.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, these practices help distinguish genuine predictive progress from evaluation artifacts. More reliable comparisons support better-informed model selection for protein–ligand binding prediction.
visual_elements: Protein–ligand binding illustration showing a ligand fitting into a protein pocket.
Train/test split diagram highlighting potential data leakage pathways.
Checklist with icons for transparent data, accessible code and documented procedures.
Side-by-side evaluation pipelines contrasting biased benchmarking with fair, reproducible comparison.
paper_title: Guidelines for evaluating structure-based methods for protein–ligand binding prediction
